task.description: Sizing/diagnosis pass on ISS-0425 (flat supervision tree, no dependency layering, empty domain-owning layer, Task.Supervisor sprawl). Re-read lib/letflow/application.ex as it exists today (2026-09-03) since REQ-214/215/216/217/218 and ISS-0429 have all merged since the issue was filed 2026-09-02, get the real current child count and Task.Supervisor count, cross-check against ISS-0421 (Poller SPOF, restart-intensity overlap) and ISS-0422 (InstanceSupervisor doc drift, explicitly docs-only), and make the WF-03 sizing call using the same bar ISS-0411/ISS-0431 were sized against. Diagnosis only -- no fix implementation, no requirement drafting.

result.summary:
CONFIRMED BY DIRECT READ of lib/letflow/application.ex as it exists today (2026-09-03), not from the issue's stale prose. The issue's own '~15 children / six Task.Supervisors' figures (filed 2026-09-02, before REQ-214/215/216/217/218 and ISS-0429 merged) are stale and the real picture is materially worse, not better.

CURRENT CHILD COUNT: the top-level `children` list plus its three gated appends (`scheduler_children/0`, `service_task_dispatcher_children/0`, `http_child/0`) now total 20 children under default (dev/prod) config: Repo, Ecto.Migrator, Oidcc.ProviderConfiguration.Worker, Registry, Letflow.Metrics.Registry, Letflow.Admission (REQ-216), Letflow.InstanceSupervisor, SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor, SandboxPool, Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor, Engine.PluginRegistry, Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistry, Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor, Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor (ISS-0429), Letflow.Scheduler.Poller, Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (REQ-214), Bandit. All still one flat list under a single `Supervisor.start_link(children, strategy: :one_for_one, name: Letflow.Supervisor)` at application.ex:139 with no `max_restarts`/`max_seconds` override -- OTP default (3 restarts/5s) unchanged since the issue was filed. Under test config (start_scheduler/start_service_task_dispatcher/start_http all false) the count drops to 17, still flat.

TASK.SUPERVISOR COUNT IS NOW SEVEN, NOT SIX: SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor, Engine.PluginTaskSupervisor, Engine.Lua.TaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleRegistryTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.CapabilityGateTaskSupervisor, Engine.Wasm.ModuleVersionRegistryTaskSupervisor, and Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor (added by ISS-0429, application.ex:133, with its own load-bearing ordering comment: MUST precede `scheduler_children()` because Poller's first :tick fires with zero delay via `Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 0)` and can dispatch to it on that very first tick). The issue's own prediction partially materialized but not via the predicted path: REQ-214 itself added a Poller (Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller), not a Task.Supervisor -- but ISS-0429 independently added the seventh Task.Supervisor the issue warned REQ-214 would add, so the sprawl concern is confirmed live, just from a different requirement. Additionally, REQ-214 copy-pasted the EXACT same documented restart-intensity hazard that scheduler_children/0's own comment describes for Letflow.Scheduler.Poller (application.ex:181-197: 'the IDENTICAL documented hazard... zero-delay first tick... raises DBConnection.OwnershipError repeatedly until this supervisor's restart intensity is exceeded and the whole application, Letflow.Repo included, shuts down') onto a second Poller, gated by a second independent config flag (`start_service_task_dispatcher`). REQ-216 (Letflow.Admission) and REQ-217/218 (wiring, no new application.ex children per ISS-0431's own resolution note) added one more peer (Letflow.Admission) with its own moduledoc reasoning for placement but, per that same moduledoc, deliberately NO ordering dependency either way -- i.e. it was added as a peer without engaging the layering question this issue raises at all, exactly the accretion pattern ISS-0425 predicts will keep recurring if left unaddressed.

ORDERING CONSTRAINTS THAT MUST SURVIVE ANY RESTRUCTURE (both verified present in application.ex today, both hand-maintained via list order with no structural enforcement): (1) SandboxPool.TaskSupervisor before {Letflow.SandboxPool, []} (ISS-0224, application.ex:67-73); (2) Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor before scheduler_children() (ISS-0429, application.ex:114-133). Both are exactly the kind of order-dependent-on-list-position hazard the issue names as the signal for explicit layering -- a `:rest_for_one` top level or layered `:one_for_one` groups would make both structural instead of comment-enforced, but ANY restructure must preserve both orderings exactly or it reintroduces the crash windows ISS-0224/ISS-0429 fixed.

ISS-0421 CROSS-CHECK (Scheduler.Poller SPOF/restart-intensity, still status: open): confirmed genuinely overlapping only on the restart-intensity question, not the tree-shape question -- ISS-0421's scope is internal to Poller (seven serial per-tenant sweeps, Task.async_stream bounding, or an explicit max_restarts/max_seconds override scoped to a Poller-owning supervisor). Per ISS-0425's own text ('whichever runs second reads the other's outcome rather than re-deciding it') and ISS-0421 is still open while ISS-0425 is being sized now, ISS-0425's design (if it proceeds) should be the one to settle the restart-intensity/layering shape, with ISS-0421 then reading that outcome for its own Poller-internal fix rather than inventing a second, possibly conflicting intensity policy. Worth flagging to REQ-ANALYST as an explicit sequencing note.

ISS-0422 CROSS-CHECK (InstanceSupervisor doc drift, still status: open): confirmed genuinely OUT of this issue's scope -- ISS-0422 is explicitly 'DOCUMENTATION ONLY' (CLAUDE.md/requirements.yaml wording drift), not an architecture change, and explicitly says not to reverse REQ-045's row-based decision. ISS-0425's concern (2), 'no supervisor owns the domain,' is a narrower, different claim: that whatever real long-lived domain process eventually needs a supervised home (REQ-214's dispatcher pattern is the first candidate) has no layer to attach to, independent of whether InstanceSupervisor's moduledoc text is accurate. These two issues do not need to be resolved together, but a layering requirement should note InstanceSupervisor's current empty-DynamicSupervisor shape as the likely (not mandatory) attachment point for that layer, consistent with REQ-045 AC5's explicit retention of it.

SIZING VERDICT, using ISS-0411/ISS-0431's own established bar (new architectural decision with no existing pattern to extend + multi-file/whole-boot-sequence scope + real risk of destabilizing existing behavior if done as an unreviewed patch => route through REQ-ANALYST rather than fix as a scoped WF-03 issue or design in a same-run CODE-DESIGNER pass): THIS IS NOT A SCOPED WF-03 FIX, and it does not fit a single same-run CODE-DESIGNER pass either, for reasons stronger than ISS-0431's own bar. (1) The issue's own suggestion ('candidate shape: :rest_for_one at the top level over layered groups') is explicitly a candidate, not a decision -- picking :rest_for_one vs. layered :one_for_one groups vs. some other shape, and deciding what restart-intensity policy applies to each layer, is a genuine open architecture question with real availability tradeoffs (rest_for_one at the top restarts every LATER-listed child when an EARLIER one crashes -- e.g. a Repo restart would cascade-restart all 19 other children under naive rest_for_one, which may be desirable or may be far too blunt depending on which layer boundary is chosen; this is not resolvable by CODE-DESIGNER unilaterally without becoming a de facto requirement, exactly ISS-0411/ISS-0431's own criterion). (2) Scope is now larger than at filing: 20 children (not 15), 7 Task.Supervisors (not 6), TWO Pollers sharing the identical zero-delay-first-tick restart-intensity hazard (not one), and a THIRD gated peer (Letflow.Admission) added with zero engagement of the layering question -- meaning any design must reconcile at least three independently-evolved config-gating patterns (start_scheduler, start_service_task_dispatcher, start_http) plus two hand-maintained, comment-only ordering constraints (ISS-0224, ISS-0429) into one coherent layered shape without breaking any of them. (3) Real, non-hypothetical blast radius: application.ex is the application's own boot sequence -- an error in a same-run design/implementation risks breaking startup for EVERY existing supervised child, not just the ones being restructured, with no independent design-validation gate to catch a wrong ordering claim before ELIXIR-DEV implements it (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR checks completeness/clarity/no-code, not runtime ordering correctness against 20 children's worth of hand-maintained constraints). (4) It bundles at least three separable, genuinely open decisions the same way ISS-0431 did: (a) top-level strategy and layer boundaries (infrastructure / domain-workers / HTTP, per the issue's own candidate shape), (b) restart-intensity policy per layer (feeds ISS-0421, which is waiting on this), (c) the Task.Supervisor consolidate-vs-justify-and-keep review (the issue itself calls this 'worth one deliberate review pass' -- a distinct, smaller-scoped decision that could land as its own AC or its own requirement).

RECOMMENDATION TO ORCH (mirroring ISS-0411/ISS-0431's own routing precedent): dispatch REQ-ANALYST to draft one or more properly-sized S6 requirements. Suggested split, for REQ-ANALYST to finalize, mirroring the ISS-0431 precedent (one core requirement plus per-surface follow-ons) rather than a single monolithic requirement given the blast-radius concern above: (a) a CORE layering requirement -- decide and implement the top-level strategy (rest_for_one vs. layered one_for_one groups) and the infrastructure/domain/http layer boundaries, with explicit ACs requiring every existing hand-maintained ordering constraint (ISS-0224's SandboxPool pair, ISS-0429's Obs.Alerts.TaskSupervisor-before-scheduler_children) to be preserved and, ideally, made structural rather than comment-enforced; this requirement should also settle restart-intensity policy per layer, explicitly named as the input ISS-0421 is waiting on; (b) a smaller follow-on requirement or AC-set applying the settled layer shape to both existing Pollers (Scheduler.Poller and ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller) so they stop being flat peers with duplicated hazard comments; (c) a Task.Supervisor review requirement or AC-set, scoped narrowly to the 'consolidate vs. justify-and-keep' decision the issue itself frames as a lighter, more contained pass (all seven currently have real per-subsystem justification on record -- REQ-ANALYST should treat 'keep all seven with one consolidated rationale doc' as an equally valid acceptance outcome to actual consolidation, per the issue's own text). REQ-ANALYST should also read ISS-0421 (open, restart-intensity-adjacent) and ISS-0422 (open, docs-only, InstanceSupervisor as likely but non-mandatory attachment point) before drafting, and should note in the new requirement(s) that ISS-0421 is deliberately sequenced to land after this one. This record (ISS-0425) should stay open, per ISS-0411/ISS-0431's own precedent, until the resulting requirement(s) are done -- closing it now would misrepresent a diagnosed-but-unfixed architectural gap as resolved.
